title: Accept DG-06A coordination boundary
outcome: The authoritative architecture contracts accept DG-06A as a workspaces-owned, use-case-specific onboarding and invitation coordination boundary with public-facade-only identity calls, composition-root governance handler registration, and explicitly owned atomic rollback and postcondition semantics, without claiming that application behavior has been implemented or proven.
scope: Record the explicitly approved DG-06A direction as an accepted architecture decision and index it among authoritative ADRs.
Specify that a workspaces-owned, use-case-specific application service coordinates first-user/workspace creation and invitation acceptance through identity's public facade.

Specify composition-root registration of governance audit handlers and one explicitly owned transaction/session covering identity, workspace, invitation or membership, and required governance audit effects with all-or-nothing rollback and postcondition semantics.
Align only the existing module manifest dependency and event-consumer edges needed to make the accepted coordination direction unambiguous.
Add one built-in-Deno deterministic architecture contract check with a passing harness self-check and a focused accepted-contract assertion.
nonGoals: Implement or claim executable onboarding, invitation, identity, membership, transaction, rollback, postcondition, or governance audit behavior.
Close or relabel a planning gate merely by editing planning proposals; executable application proof remains a dependency of the protected walking skeleton and Slice 1.
Choose an authentication implementation, migration runner, database ledger, queue, gateway, provider, dependency, or version.
Introduce a generic horizontal coordinator, direct cross-module table write, private adapter import, new schema source, or durable event infrastructure.
Modify AGENTS.md, FND-001 paths, planning proposals, product catalogs, the canonical schema bundle, .codex, .agents, or .git content.
Push, deploy, merge into main, or record the ticket as integrated.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An indexed accepted ADR assigns onboarding and invitation coordination to a workspaces-owned, use-case-specific application service, permits identity calls only through identity's public facade, assigns governance audit handler registration to the composition root, and forbids a generic horizontal coordinator, private adapter imports, and direct cross-module table writes.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: deno test --allow-read=docs/architecture tools/architecture/FND-002/coordination_contract_test.ts fails because the accepted ADR and its index entry are absent while the check's in-memory discrimination self-test passes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The backend contract assigns one workspaces-owned transaction/session boundary to first-user/workspace creation and invitation acceptance, including identity, membership, and required governance audit effects, and requires all-or-nothing rollback plus explicit success postconditions before commit.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused Deno command fails against the unchanged backend contract because the use-case-specific shared transaction ownership, rollback trigger, and postcondition requirements are absent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The machine manifest retains only the public workspaces-to-identity dependency direction for this coordinator, removes identity-driven workspace onboarding consumption, and declares governance consumption of identity.user-registered, workspace.created, and workspace.member-joined from their existing publishers without adding a coordination module or workspaces-to-governance dependency.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused Deno command fails against the unchanged manifest because workspaces still consumes identity.user-registered and governance does not consume workspace.created or workspace.member-joined.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The accepted contracts explicitly distinguish this synchronous transaction-scoped coordination from durable asynchronous delivery and state that application rollback/postcondition behavior is not implemented or proven by FND-002; protected walking-skeleton and Slice 1 executable proof remains required.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused Deno command fails because the unchanged architecture contracts do not contain the bounded proof-pending disclaimer, while its harness self-check remains green.

risks: Ambiguous event edges could retain competing identity-driven workspace choreography or omit required governance audit participation.
A documentation-only ticket could overstate atomic rollback or postcondition behavior that has not yet been implemented against PostgreSQL.
Shared transaction/session wording could be misread as permission to bypass module-owned public facades or write another module's tables directly.
Treating transaction-scoped governance handlers as durable asynchronous delivery could weaken required audit atomicity or conflict with the background-work contract.
Broadening the ticket into auth, migration, queue, provider, schema, or dependency selection would resolve choices outside the approved boundary.
